paragraphs.text:
Though you’ve fallen, you realize that you’re not completely 
without landmarks. If you follow the cliff above you, you may 
just be able to find the point where the elevation changes, and 
in doing so find your way back to the path. You limp forward in 
pain, making sure to keep the cliff face on your left.

You follow the cliff wall despite the fog, at points navigating 
purely by keeping your hand in contact with the rock face, 
occasionally stopping to lean against it for support in your 
injured state. Eventually, you manage to find the trail again, 
crying out in relief at your apparent turn of good fortune.

You move along the path for what must be an hour until 
you see a distant light piercing the fog. You rush toward it, not 
caring that you’re putting weight on your damaged leg, only to 
find yourself standing face-to-face with a brick wall.

Peering through the fog, you find that you’ve somehow 
gotten turned around and are back in Esbury. You cry out in 
frustration.

Suddenly, you hear the revving of an engine. A car comes 
hurtling toward you as you stand, despairing, in the middle of 
the road.
